summary: Identified the bad lifecycle entry as the filled_loss replay case, where the paper execution ledger filled a market that the deterministic execution fixture already marked as settled no. Added a minimal execution-ledger guardrail that blocks paper fills for fixture markets already settled to no, preserving legitimate winning fills and existing raw rejection/no-action behavior.
bad_entry_analysis: The bad entry passed because scorer and paper order planning saw the same legitimate candidate inputs as the winning BTC above 90000 cases: positive buffered edge, pass liquidity, pass spread, and low risk. The distinguishing data only existed in lifecycle execution fixture state: settled=true and settlement_outcome=no. Since that is lifecycle handling, not scorer/planner input quality, the smallest correct guardrail is in the paper execution ledger: do not fill a fixture market that is already settled no.
limitations: Fixture-only guardrail; no live markets, prices, APIs, or external metadata are fetched.
The guardrail prevents paper fills only when deterministic fixture lifecycle state already marks the market settled no.
This does not attempt to eliminate ordinary unresolved market risk or future losing paper trades that are not knowable at execution time.
No runtime integration, dispatcher/run_codex, prompt automation, credentials, wallet access, real orders, live trading, unrelated cleanup, or new validation layer was added.
recommended_next_task: PMBOT-BRAIN-014: add offline lifecycle regression gates after review approval to lock required scenario outcomes and safety flags.
